_about: Chapter 6 (Travel): Don Raúl sells a long-distance bus ticket at the terminal's window: where to, one-way or round-trip, the return day, the departure (twist: the morning bus is sold out), the seat, the ID, a student or INAPAM discount, paying, the ticket, the gate.

items.prompt: Don Raúl, the ticket clerk, sits behind the ticket window about one third from the left, both hands resting on the counter by the small opening in the glass, leaning a little toward it with a polite, slightly formal smile as the learner walks up ("¡Buenos días! ¿A dónde va?"). Beside him, a blank ticket printer and a monitor turned away from the viewer.

Change only his pose and expression: he holds up two blank paper tickets side by side at chest height behind the glass, one short and one twice as long, eyebrows raised over his glasses (one-way or round-trip?).

Change only his pose and expression: he holds up a small desk calendar with a blank grid of empty squares (no numbers, no words) toward the glass, a pen ready in his other hand, eyebrows raised (which day?).

Change only his pose and expression: he half turns in his chair and points with one finger at a round wall clock with plain tick marks and no numerals hanging on the wall behind him on the left, looking back at the learner with raised eyebrows (which departure?).

Change only his pose and expression: he winces apologetically, one hand pressed flat to his forehead and the other turned palm up in a small helpless gesture, glancing at the monitor (the morning bus is full: "¡Híjole!").

Change only his pose and expression: he holds a laminated seat-map card flat against the glass, facing the learner: a bus plan of small blank squares in two pairs of rows with an aisle between them (no numbers), his fingertip on a window seat, eyebrows raised (window or aisle?).

Change only his pose and expression: he reaches one open hand, palm up, through the small opening at the bottom of the glass, waiting politely for the learner's ID; his other hand rests on the keyboard.

Change only his pose and expression: he holds up a small blank plastic card between two fingers at the glass (only a photo square and gray lines), eyebrows raised over his glasses (a student card or a senior card?).

Change only his pose and expression: he slides a small card terminal with a blank screen through the opening in the glass toward the learner, his other hand open, waiting (cash or card), a polite smile.
Change only his pose and expression: he passes a printed paper ticket (blank, only a few gray lines and a small bus icon) through the opening toward the learner, with a warm, satisfied smile.
Change only his pose and expression: he points with his whole hand off to the left, toward the gates (andenes) where the long-distance buses leave, explaining helpfully and precisely.
Change only his pose and expression: he raises one hand in a small, friendly wave, smiling warmly ("¡Buen viaje!").
